title: Best Average Worst Case Check
description: Identify best, average, and worst cases when cost depends on input shape.

questions.prompt: For linear search, when is the best case?
questions.explanation: Best case is the most favorable input: target at index `0` → `O(1)` comparisons.

questions.prompt: Linear search worst case (missing or last element) is:
questions.explanation: Worst case is least favorable: missing or last element → `O(n)` comparisons.

questions.prompt: Why is best-case alone a weak argument for choosing an algorithm?

options.text: Best case never happens in practice
It ignores typical and adversarial inputs that matter for SLAs

questions.explanation: Worst-case guarantees matter for latency SLAs and adversarial inputs. Best-case alone is a weak argument for choosing an algorithm.

questions.prompt: Saying “average case” without context is incomplete because:

options.text: Average case always equals best case
Average needs an assumed input distribution
Average case is illegal in Big-O notation
Only worst case can use Big-O

questions.explanation: Average-case needs an assumed distribution — “average” is not magic. Clarify which case when you quote Big-O.
